audit.title: DataLink Reference (Pull Delivery)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with meta-description prose — "This section provides technical reference documentation..." — that describes the page instead of answering anything. No liftable fact about DataLink pull-delivery exists.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1/H2, 0 level skips, no oversized sections — but only 2 headings and no lists/tables because there is almost no content to structure.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 numerals, 0 units, 0 version strings. A reference page with no specifics is inert for GEO.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 1 internal link (to `llms.txt`), 0 external, 0 primary sources. No links to the actual API spec, SDK repo, or verification contract.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "DataLink pull-delivery" is used but never defined; no crisp one-sentence canonical statement engines can quote.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no `TechArticle` schema (measured). Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 fenced blocks. A page titled "Reference" covering "API, SDKs, and Onchain Verification" with zero code or endpoint signatures cannot serve an agent.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Matches no concrete "how do I…" or "what is…" query; no endpoints, params, errors, or troubleshooting.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Prose is unambiguous and grammatically clean; "DataLink" naming is consistent — but there is too little text to demonstrate more.

audit.summary: This is a 60-word section landing stub for DataLink pull-delivery reference material — it announces that API specs, SDKs, and onchain verification docs exist but contains none of them. Its only strength is clean, fluent prose; its overwhelming weakness is that it is empty of extractable technical substance (0 numerals, 0 code blocks, 0 tables, 0 definitions, no metadata), so a generative engine has nothing to lift, cite, or synthesize. As a reference page it fails the core promise in its own subtitle: it should either be built out with actual API/SDK reference content or be treated purely as a navigation node that links directly to the real reference pages. Honest verdict: not retrievable or citable in its current form.

recommendations.title: Add the actual reference content this page promises
recommendations.where: under `## API, SDKs, and Onchain Verification`
recommendations.issue: "Learn how to integrate DataLink into your applications using APIs, SDKs, and onchain verification methods."
recommendations.change: Replace the descriptive sentence with the real reference: a table of API endpoints (method, path, params, response), SDK install/version, and the onchain verifier contract address per network — each as a labeled, copy-pasteable block. If the content lives elsewhere, this page should be a link hub (below), not a stub.
recommendations.why: Numbers, params, addresses, and code are the highest-lift retrievable content; the page currently has none.

recommendations.title: Lead with a canonical definition of DataLink pull-delivery
recommendations.issue: "This section provides technical reference documentation for integrating with DataLink pull-delivery feeds."
recommendations.change: Open with a self-contained definition, e.g. "DataLink pull-delivery lets applications fetch signed offchain reports on demand and verify them onchain via the DataLink verifier contract." Then keep the navigation sentence.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim-liftable statement and defends against parametric priors when only the intro is skimmed.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased H3s that link to the real answers
recommendations.issue: No headings match how devs ask ("how do I verify a DataLink report onchain", "DataLink API authentication", "SDK reference").
recommendations.change: Add question-phrased H3s each linking to the concrete reference page: "How do I authenticate to the DataLink pull API?", "What is the onchain verifier contract address?", "Which SDKs support DataLink pull-delivery?"
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled index prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add direct links to primary reference sources
recommendations.issue: Only link on the page points to `llms.txt`; no link to API spec, SDK repo, or contract.
recommendations.change: Add inline links to the OpenAPI/API spec, the SDK package (npm/GitHub with version), and the verifier contract on a block explorer.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise citation rate and let agents follow through to executable detail.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, `inLanguage`, a self-referencing canonical URL, and a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Establishes E-E-A-T and lets agents parse/trust freshness — currently unverifiable.

antiPatterns: Wall-free but content-free: the page is a description of documentation rather than documentation ("This section provides technical reference documentation…").
Undated / no freshness signal (measured: no datePublished/dateModified).
Unfulfilled promise: subtitle claims "API specifications, and implementation details" that do not appear on the page.
offPageNotes: Site already exposes `/llms.txt` — good; ensure this URL and its child reference pages are listed there.
If the real reference content lives on sibling pages, add internal links from those pages back to this hub (canonical-hub pattern) so retrieval consolidates.
Canonical/schema may be injected at a template level not captured here — pass raw `<head>` to the CLI to confirm before treating metadata as fully absent.
